segments.text: The first warning comes at 4:17 PM.
An emergency alert fills the screen.
Avoid anyone showing signs of confusion or violent behavior.
Do not approach emergency responders unless instructed.
Outside, traffic slows to a stop.
A man stands in the middle of the road, staring at nothing.
Then, he suddenly runs at a passing car.
Someone screams and then every phone in the store starts ringing.
You're working alone at a small convenience store.
The front windows face the street.
The back door opens into a narrow delivery alley.
Then, you switch off the lights.
For a moment, the store goes silent.
Outside, a woman stands with shaking hands.
She keeps looking over her shoulder.
But behind her, across the street, a police officer slowly backs away from a group of people.
You don't know if she's sick.
You don't know if she's scared.
And you don't know what happens if you open that door.
You use your phone flashlight and check the supplies.
Two bottles of water, a few cans, one chocolate bar, a first aid kit.
Not enough to wait this out.
Then you hear a metal crash from the delivery alley.
Someone is trying the back door.
You move between the shelves and listen.
You look through the tiny window.
A shape stands outside facing the door.
Do not respond to voices coming from outside.
Some affected individuals may imitate familiar speech.
From the other side of the door, a voice calls your name.
It sounds exactly like your brother.
You haven't told anyone where you are.
For the rest of the night, you stay behind the counter, listening to footsteps move around
At sunrise, the street is empty.
A distant alarm keeps repeating the same warning.
Your phone has one bar of battery left.
You open an offline map and find the nearest underground transit station.
It has a maintenance entrance two streets away.
You pack the water, the first aid kit, and one can of food.
Then you wait until the street is quiet.
You move quickly, keeping close to the walls.
At the station entrance, you find the maintenance door hanging open.
The stairwell smells of dust and damp concrete.
Somewhere below, a radio is playing.
At the bottom, you find a man sitting beside a young boy.
The man raises one finger to his lips.
The man beside him goes pale.
He slowly turns toward the boy.
Your dad never used that radio.
This time, the voice is clearer.
You turn toward the dark tunnel.
Then, from somewhere deep underground, you hear a child's voice call out.
The boy beside you grabs your sleeve.
And then, the radio switches off.
Behind you, the maintenance door begins to close.
